papers.title: Clinician-AI Collaboration in Endovascular Neurointerventions: In-Vitro User Study of Copilot Assistance Modes for Robotic Navigation Across the Autonomy Spectrum
papers.summary: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an effective treatment for acute ischemic stroke, yet access remains limited by the availability of specialist neurointerventional expertise. Telerobotic and AI-assisted systems may help address this challenge, but it remains unclear how clinicians interact with different levels of autonomy and how autonomous navigation systems perform in clinically realistic environments. papers.title: Liquid Robots: Non‐Equilibrium Assemblies Catching, Handing Over and Positioning Oil Droplets Along Arrays
papers.summary: Interacting droplets provide a promising route toward adaptive matter capable of autonomous transport, organization and reconfiguration. Realizing such systems, however, requires mechanisms that balance attractive and repulsive forces without continuous external control. Here, we present a liquid robotic platform based on filamentous assemblies that, analogous to handover processes in conventional robotic systems, can capture, transfer, and position cargo droplets. papers.title: Bridging the institutional STEM divide: A multi-strand evaluation of a hands-on workshop for students from public and private schools in Ecuador
papers.summary: The STEM performance gap between public and private educational institutions in Ecuador represents a persistent challenge for educational equity. This study evaluated the impact of a 10-day hands-on robotics and technology workshop in Cuenca, Ecuador, through a quasi-experimental design structured across three complementary analytical strands. Strand 1 ( N = 114 ) utilized a pre-test/post-test design with ANCOVA to measure conceptual knowledge convergence. papers.summary: The advancement of digital technology and generative artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed the creation of electronic documents and signatures. Although the Electronic Information and Transactions (EIT) Law and its implementing regulations have legally recognized electronic documents and signatures as valid evidence, the conventional civil procedural evidence system faces severe challenges. These challenges stem from the rise of document falsification, the threat of deepfakes, and the risk of exploiting AI-manipulation claims to evade legal liability (the liar's dividend).

Realizing two-qubit gates on this platform is a critical step towards practical quantum information processing. papers.title: Multimodal motion and behavior switching of multistable ciliary walkers
papers.summary: The collective motion of arrays of cilia-tiny, hairlike protrusions-drives the locomotion of numerous microorganisms, enabling multimodal motion and switching between gaits to navigate complex environments. Inspired by this multimodal motion, we introduce multistable soft walkers with millimeter-scale flexible cilia that buckle under the walkers weight, coupling multistability and actuation within a single physical mechanism. papers.title: Shared control/autonomy in human-robot interaction: Current trends and the role of generative AI
papers.summary: In shared control and shared autonomy (SC/SA) systems, humans collaborate with robot agents to achieve common goals. Such systems enable collaborations beyond what either agent could do alone, benefiting from the relative strengths of humans (e.g., reasoning, planning) and robots (e.g., precision, repeatability). Research in this area dates back over 40 years, with numerous applications, such as in manufacturing, robot-assisted surgery, and assistive technologies. papers.summary: Introduction Socially assistive robots hold promise for supporting paediatric therapy, but adapting them to healthcare practice requires attention to therapeutic goals, professional responsibilities, and local workflows. Using Mobirobot as a case, this paper examines how an interprofessional development process was organised across inpatient sports therapy, inpatient physiotherapy, and outpatient physiotherapy, and how stakeholder input from these settings was translated into changes to the robot and its use. papers.summary: Inspired by biology’s use of vesicles for targeted transport, many studies have propelled liposomes with active matter, creating synthetic systems that can be viewed as microscale biohybrid robots. papers.summary: Understanding how carbon emissions are structurally generated within production systems remains a central challenge in environmental accounting. papers.title: Reversible nonrelativistic magnon spin transport in ferroelastic altermagnets
papers.summary: Magnons in antiferromagnetic (AFM) insulators facilitate low-dissipation, stray-field-free spin transport. papers.title: Optimizing Landau-Zener-Stückelberg-Majorana protocol for high-fidelity gates in open-system fluxonium
papers.summary: Quantum gates based on resonant Rabi oscillations are inherently slow for small-frequency qubits. They are also prone to errors due to counter-rotating terms. papers.summary: Lateral surface cooling can limit temperature rise in lithium-ion batteries through its large heat-transfer area, whereas tab cooling can reduce internal thermal gradients by exploiting the high thermal conductivity of the current collectors. papers.title: Magnetic ionic liquids: synthesis, properties and applications
papers.summary: By combining the tunability and little volatility of ionic liquids with magnetic responsiveness, magnetic ionic liquids (MILs) have become multipurpose materials that provide easy magnetic manipulation, separation, and recovery. With a focus on the connections between molecular structure, magnetic response, viscosity, transport properties, stability, and functional performance, this review critically explores recent developments in the design, synthesis, physicochemical properties, and applications of MILs.
